messages.content: I have had a scratchy throat and low fever (99.8°F) since yesterday morning.

Thank you for sharing your symptoms. Based on your description of a scratchy throat and low fever (99.8°F), this presents typical viral upper respiratory signs. A General Physician can examine your pharynx and verify whether symptom relief measures are sufficient.

triage.summary: Reported onset of scratchy throat and mild fever (99.8°F) for ~24 hours.
triage.reasons_for_specialty: A General Physician can safely differentiate between common viral pharyngitis and bacterial strep throat, recommending appropriate gargles or antipyretics.
triage.explanation: Most low-grade fevers with throat discomfort are self-limiting viral episodes, but require clinical evaluation if temperature spikes or breathing is affected.
next_steps: Warm saline gargles 3-4 times a day
Monitor body temperature using an oral digital thermometer twice daily
warning_signs: Difficulty swallowing saliva or opening mouth (trismus)
Persistent high fever above 102°F exceeding 3 days
triage.disclaimer: MediMate AI provides triage guidance and health education. It does not replace clinical diagnosis. In emergencies, call 112.
